name: ParsGen
description: Gender identification from text remains a challenging task in low-resource languages, where scarce annotated data and rich morphological variations limit model performance. This study presents a systematic evaluation of gender prediction in Persian social media, contributing to the field of Artificial Intelligence (AI) by benchmarking classical machine learning, embedding-based methods, transformer architectures, and Large Language Models (LLMs) against human performance. To enable this investigation, we introduce ParsGen, a rigorously annotated Persian gender identification dataset comprising 20,877 users and over 200,000 tweets. From an engineering perspective, this work provides a robust framework for automated author profiling, which is essential for developing personalized systems and enhancing digital forensic tools in low-resource environments.Our results reveal that machines now consistently outperform human annotators. Domain-adapted transformer models dominate traditional baselines, with a specialized model (further pre-trained on Persian political tweets) achieving a 64.76% macro F1-score on the Single-Tweet task. When ten tweets per user are available, a fine-tuned Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) model reaches a new state-of-the-art of 83.93% macro F1-score, surpassing both zero-shot LLMs and non-expert human judgments. We demonstrate near-linear performance gains with increasing tweet volume, highlighting a generalizable principle for low-resource author profiling. ParsGen is publicly available on request, providing an essential benchmark for future research on gender inference and responsible AI in engineering applications.
typical_sota_score: 65–84% (macro F1) depending on scenario: ~64.8% for single-tweet, ~83.9% for 10-tweet user-level setups reported by the authors
reputation: A valuable, language-specific benchmark for Persian author profiling that has been cited in low-resource NLP studies; adoption is growing within Persian NLP and forensic profiling research.
notes: Language-specific (Persian) dataset (~20k users, >200k tweets) with social sensitivity and privacy concerns for gender inference tasks. Dataset is available on request (not fully public). Potential label noise, demographic bias, and contamination risk if models were pre-trained on overlapping social-media data; non-LLM baselines and LLM evaluations reported.
